title: Revelation 8 — The seventh seal: silence in heaven + the first four trumpets

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

verdicts.reasoning: Kai hotan ēnoixen ... egeneto sigē en tō ouranō hōs hēmiōrion. hotan + aorist indicative noted; literal line as the central cosmic-silence entry prescribes. Reception note accurately states the canon does not quote 8:1 and reads the seventh seal as the final atomic cataclysm (LWTE-2:160); no leakage.
tous hepta angelous hoi enōpion tou theou hestēkasin, kai edothēsan autois hepta salpinges. Exact; Tob 12:15 / 1 En 20 kept as background.

libanōton chrysoun 'golden censer'; hina dōsei (future after hina) tais proseuchais 'that he should add it to the prayers' (ASV). The dative's range ('add to' / 'offer with') is noted; the ASV choice is defensible.
anebē ho kapnos tōn thymiamatōn tais proseuchais ... enōpion tou theou; dative of accompaniment 'with the prayers'. Exact.

eilēphen (perfect) ... egemisen ... ebalen eis tēn gēn; brontai kai phōnai kai astrapai kai seismos. 'voices' (ASV) for phōnai is defensible and keeps the book's phōnē chain; 'sounds/rumblings' noted.
hoi hepta angeloi hoi echontes tas hepta salpingas hētoimasan autous hina salpisōsin. Exact; blank commentary acceptable for plain narrative.

citations: SBLGNT (Holmes 2010): no variant marker at 'kai to triton tēs gēs katekaē', i.e. Westcott-Hort, Tregelles, the NIV Greek text and Robinson-Pierpont (Byzantine majority text) all print the clause
LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:161: FR has the clause, EN follows the KJV)
verdicts.reasoning: English line approved: chalaza kai pyr memigmena en haimati, kai eblēthē (sg.) ... to triton tēs gēs katekaē is exactly rendered. Commentary fix only: the note says 'The Byzantine text behind the Textus Receptus and the KJV omits it', but the SBLGNT apparatus registers no disagreement here from Robinson-Pierpont, so the Byzantine majority text has the clause and the omission is a Textus Receptus (minority) reading. Proposed wording: 'The Textus Receptus and the KJV omit it, with a minority of manuscripts; the clause stands in the Byzantine majority text as well, and its loss is probably a homoeoteleuton, since three successive clauses end in katekaē.' The reception note is accurate (LWTE-2:161-163) and confined to the labelled paragraph.
kai hōs oros mega pyri kaiomenon eblēthē eis tēn thalassan: the visionary hōs is kept as 'something like a great mountain'. Reception note verified (LWTE-2:164-167); no leakage.
apethane to triton tōn ktismatōn ... ta echonta psychas ... diephtharēsan. 'those that had life' (ASV/KJV) is exact; constructio ad sensum noted.
epesen ek tou ouranou astēr megas kaiomenos hōs lampas: 'star', 'torch'. Literal. Reception note (missiles; LWTE-2:171) accurate and confined to the note.
to onoma tou asteros legetai ho Apsinthos ... egeneto to triton tōn hydatōn eis apsinthon ... epikranthēsan. Exact; 'people' for anthrōpoi matches 6:4.

eplēgē to triton tou hēliou ... hina skotisthē to triton autōn kai hē hēmera mē phanē to triton autēs, kai hē nyx homoiōs. The line keeps the ambiguity (loss of brightness vs shortened day), as the ASV does. Reception note (LWTE-2:172-174) accurate; no leakage.

citations: SBLGNT (no variant marker at henos aetou; Robinson-Pierpont agrees)
verdicts.reasoning: henos aetou petomenou en mesouranēmati: 'an eagle' (SBLGNT, NA28, and the Byzantine majority text, as the SBLGNT apparatus confirms); TR angelou correctly reported. ouai + accusative and 'remaining blasts of the trumpet' exact.

citations: SBLGNT (Holmes 2010) variant markers at Rev 16:18 and 21:3, and their absence at 8:7, 10:4, 12:17, 16:7, 21:2
Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994)
glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type direct is right: the entry declares which text is translated and how variants are reported. Three accuracy fixes. (1) The 8:7 omission is a Textus Receptus (minority) reading, not that of the Byzantine majority text, which the SBLGNT apparatus shows agreeing with SBLGNT; rephrase wherever 'Byzantine' is said there. (2) Add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou, quoted by the canon's English) to the wohChoice list of KJV-wording variants, and 16:18 (NA28 singular anthrōpos egeneto; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'). (3) Add REV-WOH-16:18's NA28 divergence to the 'NA28 bracketed or divergent readings reported' sentence. The decision itself stands.

citations: LXX usage: kyrios for the Tetragrammaton, theos for ʾĕlōhîm
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct: theos never renders the Tetragrammaton in the LXX or NT, the canon's French reads 'Dieu' at every site, and published chapters 1, 4, 6 use 'God'. The canon's English 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' is recorded in reception notes without entering the line.

Direct is defensible: at 8:9 and 16:3 the psychai are sea creatures, and psychē zōēs reproduces nep̄eš ḥayyâ. 'every living being' matches RSV/NRSV in sense. Non-blocking: the 16:3 TR variant zōsa (KJV 'every living soul') could be named in the rationale.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 146 verses, the 10 overlay entries touched and the 13 diff ops were formed from the chapters, the SBLGNT sources (including the sigla-bearing Rev.txt in the scratchpad), the overlay, the diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-r2-editor-report.md. After reading the report, no verdict changed. The report's Founder point C lists the KJV-wording variants named in commentary (8:7, 9:13, 10:4, 21:2, 21:3 'his people ... their God', 21:4). It omits 21:3 'out of heaven', which confirms the reviewer's 21:3 revise. Its 9:13 request ('the Reviewer should verify this against the NA28 apparatus') was met as far as possible: the SBLGNT marker confirms a collated edition reads tessarōn, and the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger. The printed NA28 apparatus was not available, so this is recorded as unverified at the sigla level, not as a defect. The report's 'All other lines are the Translator's draft, unchanged' was confirmed by diffing against the rev_r2 backup: only 16:3 and 16:9 differ.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-theion-sulfur: Endorse. LXX theion = gophrit (Gen 19:24), BDAG 'sulfur', NRSV 'sulfur' at all four sites; the central entry already renders the Revelation lake passages 'sulfur'. The canon's English 'brimstone' (9:18) is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Complete the inventory: add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou) and 16:18 (NA28 singular; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'); correct 8:7 to say the omission is a TR reading, not the Byzantine majority's. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-names-and-scope-rule: Endorse, and support promotion to a central Greek-NT convention. Add the explicit criterion (apply where the central English is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme; background where it imports a Hebrew-specific form), which explains chayyot at 7:11 and gophrit for theion.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-exousia: Endorse. The context rule follows BDAG's sense division and RSV/NRSV practice; 16:9 'authority over' aligns with 6:8 and 13:7. Uniform 'authority' would read badly at 9:10, 19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-16:3-living-being: Endorse. 'soul' for sea creatures imports a personal sense; 'living being' keeps the noun and the nep̄eš ḥayyâ echo.
founderDecisionRecommendations.G-doulos-servants: Endorse. Keeps the signed-off 1:1/6:11 and the canon's English 'servants'; the French 'esclaves' is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.H-pit-of-the-abyss: Endorse. ASV structure; matches the canon's French 'le puits de l'abîme'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.I-Har-magedon: Endorse. ASV form, follows the SBLGNT/NA28 rough breathing, keeps har visible without deciding the etymology.
founderDecisionRecommendations.J-12:18-versification: Endorse. P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read estathē, and SBLGNT/NA28 number it 12:18 (Metzger on 12:18). The ASV 13:1a alignment is a tooling task (orchestrator follow-up 2), not a translation issue.

reviewerReport.summary: 13 verdicts: 12 approve, 1 revise (8:7 commentary: the Textus Receptus omission is not the Byzantine majority's, since the SBLGNT apparatus shows Robinson-Pierpont has the clause; the English line is approved).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅταν ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐγένετο σιγὴ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὡς ἡμιώριον.
paragraphs.translit: kai hotan ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn hebdomēn, egeneto sigē en tō ouranō hōs hēmiōrion.

i18n.en: And when he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.

notes.official:
*Kai hotan ēnoixen* 'And when he opened': *hotan* with the aorist indicative is a Koine irregularity for *hote*. *egeneto sigē en tō ouranō hōs hēmiōrion* 'there was silence in heaven for about half an hour'. The silence echoes the prophetic call to be silent before YHWH at his judgement (Hab 2:20; Zeph 1:7; Zech 2:13) and the Jewish tradition that the heavenly praise falls silent so that Israel's prayers may be heard (cf. b. Ḥag. 12b; Bauckham, *The Climax of Prophecy*, 1993, 70-83, who links it with the incense of vv 3-5). The line is literal, as the central `cosmic-silence-shem-ha-mephorash-revelation-tradition-cross-corpus-shiur-qomah-revelation-8-1` prescribes.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) does not quote this verse but reads the seventh seal as the final cataclysm, a worldwide atomic war ending in the destruction of all life on Earth, and quotes the trumpets that follow (8:7-12; 9:1-19) as its stages. The line renders the Greek literally and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλους οἳ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἑστήκασιν, καὶ ἐδόθησαν αὐτοῖς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγες.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon tous hepta angelous hoi enōpion tou theou hestēkasin, kai edothēsan autois hepta salpinges.

i18n.en: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

notes.official: *tous hepta angelous hoi enōpion tou theou hestēkasin* 'the seven angels who stand before God': the article presupposes a known group, the seven angels of the presence of Jewish tradition (Tob 12:15 'one of the seven holy angels'; 1 En 20:1-8, seven names in the Greek), collected in the central `seven-archangels-list-1-enoch-20-tob-12-rev-8-cross-corpus` (background). *salpinges* 'trumpets': the trumpet is the signal of war and of the day of YHWH (Joel 2:1; Zeph 1:16).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἦλθεν καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἔχων λιβανωτὸν χρυσοῦν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ θυμιάματα πολλὰ ἵνα δώσει ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων πάντων ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν τὸ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai allos angelos ēlthen kai estathē epi tou thysiastēriou echōn libanōton chrysoun, kai edothē autō thymiamata polla hina dōsei tais proseuchais tōn hagiōn pantōn epi to thysiastērion to chrysoun to enōpion tou thronou.

i18n.en: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, that he should add it to the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar that is before the throne.

notes.official: *libanōton chrysoun* 'a golden censer': *libanōtos* normally means 'frankincense', and its use for the vessel is unusual (BDAG). *hina dōsei tais proseuchais tōn hagiōn pantōn* 'that he should add it to the prayers of all the saints': the bare dative can mean 'give to', i.e. add to (ASV), or 'offer with' (RSV 'to mingle with'). The ASV is kept, and v 4 (*tais proseuchais* 'with the prayers') shows the two rising together. *dōsei* is a future indicative after *hina*, a Koine usage. The golden altar before the throne is the heavenly counterpart of the incense altar of the tabernacle (Ex 30:1-10), named again at 9:13. Incense as prayer: Ps 141:2; Rev 5:8.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ καπνὸς τῶν θυμιαμάτων ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai anebē ho kapnos tōn thymiamatōn tais proseuchais tōn hagiōn ek cheiros tou angelou enōpion tou theou.

i18n.en: And the smoke of the incense went up with the prayers of the saints from the hand of the angel before God.

notes.official: *tais proseuchais* 'with the prayers': dative of accompaniment. The smoke rises *enōpion tou theou* 'before God', a sign that the prayers are received.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἴληφεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸν λιβανωτόν, καὶ ἐγέμισεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένοντο βρονταὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ ἀστραπαὶ καὶ σεισμός.
paragraphs.translit: kai eilēphen ho angelos ton libanōton, kai egemisen auton ek tou pyros tou thysiastēriou, kai ebalen eis tēn gēn· kai egenonto brontai kai phōnai kai astrapai kai seismos.

i18n.en: And the angel took the censer and filled it with the fire of the altar and cast it onto the earth; and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake.

notes.official: *eilēphen* 'took' is a perfect in narrative sequence. The censer filled with fire from the altar and cast onto the earth comes from Ezek 10:2, where coals from among the cherubim are scattered over Jerusalem. *brontai kai phōnai kai astrapai kai seismos* 'thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake' is the Sinai theophany (Ex 19:16-18), which Revelation repeats with growing intensity at 4:5, 8:5, 11:19 and 16:18 (Bauckham, *The Climax of Prophecy*, 1993, 202-204). *phōnai* can also be 'sounds' or 'rumblings' (NRSV); 'voices' (ASV) keeps the link with *phōnē* 'voice' throughout the book.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγας ἡτοίμασαν αὑτοὺς ἵνα σαλπίσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi hepta angeloi hoi echontes tas hepta salpingas hētoimasan hautous hina salpisōsin.

i18n.en: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένετο χάλαζα καὶ πῦρ μεμιγμένα ἐν αἵματι, καὶ ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς γῆς κατεκάη, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν δένδρων κατεκάη, καὶ πᾶς χόρτος χλωρὸς κατεκάη.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho prōtos esalpisen· kai egeneto chalaza kai pyr memigmena en haimati, kai eblēthē eis tēn gēn· kai to triton tēs gēs katekaē, kai to triton tōn dendrōn katekaē, kai pas chortos chlōros katekaē.

i18n.en: And the first sounded, and there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and it was cast onto the earth; and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees was burned up, and all green grass was burned up.

notes.official:
*kai to triton tēs gēs katekaē* 'and a third of the earth was burned up' is printed by the SBLGNT and NA28 without any variant marker and is read by the major uncials and by the Byzantine majority text. The Textus Receptus and the KJV omit it with a minority of manuscripts, probably by homoeoteleuton, since three successive clauses end in *katekaē*. The line translates the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). *eblēthē* is singular, 'it was cast', treating the hail and fire as one mass (ASV 'they were cast'). The first trumpet repeats the seventh Egyptian plague, hail mingled with fire (Ex 9:23-25), with the blood of the first (Ex 7:20); cf. 'blood and fire' in Joel 3:3 LXX (2:30). The fraction 'a third', which runs through the trumpets, limits the judgement (cf. Ezek 5:2, 12; Zech 13:8-9). *chortos chlōros* 'green grass'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse. Its English edition follows the KJV and lacks 'a third of the earth was burned up'; its French original has the clause ('le tiers de la terre a été brûlé'). It reads the burning as radioactivity, after which trees and green grass no longer grow. The line follows the critical text, which here agrees with the canon's French, and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ὡς ὄρος μέγα πυρὶ καιόμενον ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῆς θαλάσσης αἷμα,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho deuteros angelos esalpisen· kai hōs oros mega pyri kaiomenon eblēthē eis tēn thalassan· kai egeneto to triton tēs thalassēs haima,

i18n.en: And the second angel sounded, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood,

notes.official:
*kai hōs oros mega pyri kaiomenon* 'and something like a great mountain burning with fire': *hōs* marks a visionary comparison, so the text does not say that a mountain fell. Cf. Jer 51:25, Babylon as 'a burnt mountain', and 1 En 18:13; 21:3, stars 'like great burning mountains'. The sea turned to blood repeats the first Egyptian plague (Ex 7:20-21).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 8-9 and reads the burning mountain as an enormous eruption of lava, produced by an atomic explosion, running into the ocean and destroying a third of marine life and of the ships. The line keeps the visionary *hōs* 'something like' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπέθανε τὸ τρίτον τῶν κτισμάτων τῶν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν πλοίων διεφθάρησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apethane to triton tōn ktismatōn tōn en tē thalassē, ta echonta psychas, kai to triton tōn ploiōn diephtharēsan.

i18n.en: and a third of the creatures that were in the sea, those that had life, died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.

notes.official: *ta echonta psychas* 'those that had life' qualifies *tōn ktismatōn* 'the creatures'. *psychē* is here the life of a living creature, as in Gen 1:20-21 LXX, not the 'soul' of a person (`psyche-soul-life-living-being-rendering-revelation`). The plural verb *diephtharēsan* 'were destroyed' with the singular *to triton* is a construction according to sense.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀστὴρ μέγας καιόμενος ὡς λαμπάς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ποταμῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tritos angelos esalpisen· kai epesen ek tou ouranou astēr megas kaiomenos hōs lampas, kai epesen epi to triton tōn potamōn kai epi tas pēgas tōn hydatōn.

i18n.en: And the third angel sounded, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of the waters.

notes.official:
*astēr megas kaiomenos hōs lampas* 'a great star ... burning like a torch': *lampas* is a torch (ASV 'lamp'). A star falling from heaven is a familiar image of judgement and of fallen powers (Isa 14:12; 1 En 86:1; 88:1). *epi tas pēgas tōn hydatōn* 'on the springs of the waters'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 10-11 and reads the 'great burning stars' as missiles falling in retaliation, polluting the drinking water and killing many who drink it. The line renders *astēr* 'star' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀστέρος λέγεται· ὁ Ἄψινθος. καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὑδάτων εἰς ἄψινθον, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέθανον ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων, ὅτι ἐπικράνθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai to onoma tou asteros legetai· ho apsinthos. kai egeneto to triton tōn hydatōn eis apsinthon, kai polloi tōn anthrōpōn apethanon ek tōn hydatōn, hoti epikranthēsan.

i18n.en: And the name of the star is called Wormwood. And a third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.

notes.official: *ho Apsinthos* 'Wormwood': the masculine article turns the plant name into a personal name. Wormwood (Heb. *laʿănâ*) is the Hebrew Bible's figure of bitterness and judgement: 'I will feed them with wormwood, and give them poisoned water to drink' (Jer 9:15; 23:15; cf. Deut 29:18; Amos 5:7). *epikranthēsan* 'they had been made bitter' reverses the sweetening of the bitter waters of Marah (Ex 15:23-25). *tōn anthrōpōn* 'people' (ASV 'men').

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐπλήγη τὸ τρίτον τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς σελήνης καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων, ἵνα σκοτισθῇ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ ἡμέρα μὴ φάνῃ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῆς, καὶ ἡ νὺξ ὁμοίως.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tetartos angelos esalpisen· kai eplēgē to triton tou hēliou kai to triton tēs selēnēs kai to triton tōn asterōn, hina skotisthē to triton autōn kai hē hēmera mē phanē to triton autēs, kai hē nyx homoiōs.

i18n.en: And the fourth angel sounded, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them was darkened, and a third of the day did not shine, and likewise the night.

notes.official:
*eplēgē* 'was struck' (ASV 'smitten') is the verb of *plēgē* 'plague'. The darkness repeats the ninth Egyptian plague (Ex 10:21-23) and the darkening of the luminaries on the day of YHWH (Joel 2:10; 3:15; Amos 8:9). *hina skotisthē to triton autōn kai hē hēmera mē phanē to triton autēs* 'so that a third of them was darkened, and a third of the day did not shine': the clause can describe a loss of brightness or a shortened day and night. The line, like the ASV, keeps both open (Aune, WBC 52B). The central `inshiqaq-al-qamar-splitting-of-the-moon-sura-54-1-multiple-readings-preserved-cross-corpus` names this verse as a comparison (background).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse and reads the darkening as the dust and ash raised by successive nuclear explosions, so thick that sun, moon and stars are hidden and day and night seem shorter. The line renders the Greek literally and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἀετοῦ πετομένου ἐν μεσουρανήματι λέγοντος φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Οὐαὶ οὐαὶ οὐαὶ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῶν λοιπῶν φωνῶν τῆς σάλπιγγος τῶν τριῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν μελλόντων σαλπίζειν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon, kai ēkousa henos aetou petomenou en mesouranēmati legontos phōnē megalē· ouai ouai ouai tous katoikountas epi tēs gēs ek tōn loipōn phōnōn tēs salpingos tōn triōn angelōn tōn mellontōn salpizein.

i18n.en: And I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in midheaven, saying with a loud voice: "Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the remaining blasts of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to sound!"

notes.official: *henos aetou* 'an eagle' is the reading of the SBLGNT and NA28, with Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the majority of manuscripts; the Textus Receptus reads *angelou* (KJV 'an angel flying through the midst of heaven'). The line translates the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). *heis* 'one' serves as an indefinite article, a Semitic usage. *en mesouranēmati* 'in midheaven': the zenith, where all can hear. The eagle as herald of judgement: Hos 8:1; Hab 1:8. *Ouai ouai ouai tous katoikountas* 'Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell': *ouai* with the accusative is a Revelation idiom (cf. 12:12), and the three woes correspond to the last three trumpets (9:12; 11:14). 'Those who dwell on the earth' is the book's term for humanity in its opposition to God (3:10; 6:10; 13:8). *ek tōn loipōn phōnōn tēs salpingos* 'because of the remaining blasts of the trumpet': *phōnē* with a trumpet is its sound (BDAG *phōnē* 1; ASV 'the other voices of the trumpet').
